behavior_in_task_description.explanation: instruction.md's 'Expected' section enumerates, in plain language, every behavior the f2p tests check: held in front of Tux, thrown the way he is walking, falls past coins as if they weren't there, knocks out an enemy it lands on, stays on top of the ground once landed, and is solid (Tux can stand on it / can't walk through it). Each maps 1:1 onto one of the 7 f2p tests in config.json. The task deliberately withholds file/function names and which specific behaviors are broken, but that omission is the intended difficulty (per task.toml's difficulty_explanation) and resolvable from the attached video, not an undocumented test requirement.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: All behaviors named in instruction.md's expected section are covered by rock_behaviour_test.cpp: carrying position, throw direction, falling past touchables (coins), landing and staying put, standing on a resting rock, being blocked by a resting rock, and knocking out an enemy on impact. p2p tests add further non-regression coverage (carry tracking, put-down landing, stacking) that is consistent with, not contradictory to, the described expectations.

informative_test_structure.explanation: tests/rock_behaviour_test.cpp is organized into clearly commented sections ('Dropping a rock past coins', 'Carrying', 'Throwing', 'A rock lying on the ground is solid', 'A rock falling on an enemy'), uses descriptive TEST names and helper functions (Scene, throw_while_walking, frames_until_on_floor) with doc comments, and every assertion carries a descriptive failure message explaining what was expected and the actual measured value.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: Bug patches are copied to a temp path, applied, and deleted within the same Dockerfile RUN layer, so they never appear in the final image's layers; tests/ and solution/ are never COPYed into the image (only bugs/ and assets/recording.mp4 are); the git history is reset and re-initialized from the post-bug state so the real upstream fix commit is unreachable; test.sh restores any test-protected paths from the immutable harbor_base tag before applying the hidden test.patch, preventing the agent from tampering with the test harness. The video is a headless recording from the task's own buggy build, not a leak of exact numeric thresholds used by the tests.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task requires fixing C++ game logic in the existing repository; it does not ask the agent to produce any structured output file (JSON/CSV/API), so no schema documentation is required.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The repository is checked out at an exact 40-character base commit SHA (and submodules are pinned transitively via that checkout), and the injected bug patches are tracked file diffs applied deterministically. Only apt packages are installed, which per the grading guidance generally need not be pinned; there are no unpinned pip/npm-style dependencies in the build.

typos.explanation: Cross-checked paths and identifiers across instruction.md, Dockerfile, test.sh, config.json, and verifier.py (e.g. /app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4 path matches between instruction.md and the Dockerfile COPY destination; test names in test.patch exactly match config.json's f2p/p2p lists; sha256 hash length is correct at 64 hex chars). No typos found that would break commands or references.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile's only COPY instructions bring in bugs/ (deleted in the same layer after being applied) and assets/recording.mp4; tests/ and solution/ directories are never copied into the built image.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: All dependencies needed to compile and run the gtest-based test binary (SDL2, googletest via submodule, boost, etc.) are legitimate build dependencies of the project itself (BUILD_TESTS=ON is a standard CMake option of this repo), not task-specific test-only tooling bolted onto the image. No separate test-only package manager (pip/npm) install happens at image build time; test.sh only reconfigures/rebuilds using libraries already present from the normal project build.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solution/fix.patch contains the actual multi-file source code fix (corrected offset math, corrected throw-direction logic, restored collision group transitions, removal of a buggy collides() override, and a corrected tile-attribute check), mirroring the real upstream PR. solve.sh applies this patch via git apply/patch rather than writing out any expected test result or output value.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: This is a source-code bug-fix task verified by compiling and running hidden C++ unit tests against the repository; the agent is not required to produce any specific named output file, so there is nothing to reference in instruction.md on this axis.
